plan.planning_summary: This control axis tests whether a hybrid perturbation strategy on a fixed 22-layer ZnS/MgF2 alternating stack can improve dual-band infrared filter performance. The prior knowledge is that quarter-wave stacks with asymmetric layer tuning can separate passbands while maintaining stopband rejection. This route uses only model prior knowledge with no literature retrieval.

routes.title: Hybrid Perturbation on 22-Layer ZnS/MgF2 Dual-Band IR Filter
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Applying wider perturbation bounds to the front half of the stack (layers 1-12) while restricting the back half (layers 13-22) to narrow local adjustments will improve the dual-band transmittance score without degrading stopband rejection, compared to uniform perturbation across all layers.
routes.design_principle: In multilayer interference filters, the front layers primarily control impedance matching and overall transmission, while the back layers fine-tune spectral positioning. Asymmetric perturbation allows global exploration where it matters most while preventing phase disruption in the terminating layers.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | Daimon-20 substrate (22 layers total, alternating high/low index)
design_variables: Individual layer thicknesses for all 22 layers
Perturbation bounds: layers 1-12 at ±8% global exploration, layers 13-22 at ±5% with ±3 nm maximum displacement cap from iteration 08 seed
soft_objectives: Maximize mean transmittance in 4.15-4.35 μm band
Maximize mean transmittance in 4.55-4.75 μm band
Minimize mean transmittance in 3.60-4.00 μm band
Minimize mean transmittance in 4.85-5.20 μm band
manufacturing_considerations: All layers must be depositable by conventional PVD or CVD methods
Total layer count fixed at 22 (within 24-layer limit)
Thicknesses should remain in practical deposition range (50-1000 nm)
theory_basis: Recalled knowledge: Quarter-wave stacks produce high reflectance at design wavelength; deviating from quarter-wave can create transmission windows
Recalled knowledge: ZnS has high refractive index (~2.2-2.4) in mid-IR and is transparent through 5 μm
Recalled knowledge: MgF2 has low refractive index (~1.3-1.4) and reasonable transmission in 4-5 μm range though absorption increases beyond 4 μm
Recalled knowledge: Daimon-20 dataset provides CaF2 substrate optical constants in 3-5 μm range
Recalled knowledge: Front layers in a stack affect impedance matching more than back layers, which primarily tune phase
expected_advantages: Hybrid perturbation should find better local optima than uniform bounds
Restricting back layers prevents destructive interference pattern shifts
Front layer exploration can improve overall transmission efficiency
Builds on iteration 08 best result (target score 0.698) as seed
known_risks: MgF2 absorption coefficient at 4-5 μm is uncertain from memory; actual k values may reduce transmission more than expected
Daimon-20 dataset selection was required because generic CaF2 name matched 4 datasets equally; this specific dataset may not match all prior iteration assumptions
The ±3 nm cap on layers 13-22 may be too restrictive if iteration 08 seed is not near optimum
ZnS stress and adhesion properties not verified; may affect manufacturability
What would settle this: Look up measured n/k data for MgF2 and ZnS at 4-5 μm from handbook or vendor data sheets

Stack sequence: ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2 (22 layers total). Initialize thicknesses from iteration 08 best candidate: [897.2128783342998, 927.7243962133199, 517.2144549592246, 923.3881401125151, 928.7521051853196, 669.4261405190617, 67.78584356432049, 112.29941644509945, 458.75081585145244, 957.6078300094041, 994.3519148417982, 966.2470589185659, 377.1979812854105, 255.38804087140915, 582.91923145124, 246.55290266788114, 825.8573574544129, 990.9340803979848, 968.8554793206682, 937.3731639376689, 193.41503851247, 556.5186678474654] nm. Apply hybrid perturbation: layers 1-12 allow ±8% thickness variation, layers 13-22 allow ±5% variation capped at ±3 nm maximum displacement from seed. Wavelength range 3500-5300 nm. Optimize for high transmittance in 4150-4350 nm and 4550-4750 nm bands, low transmittance in 3600-4000 nm and 4850-5200 nm bands. Use coherent thin-film matrix method. No metal layers. Maximum 22 layers fixed.

It is the control arm of a controlled comparison against the literature-grounded routes, and its evidence-id allowlist is empty by construction.
unresolved_decisions: Exact MgF2 extinction coefficient at 4.5-5.0 μm not known from memory; registry data will determine actual absorption
Daimon-20 substrate refractive index dispersion in 3.5-5.5 μm range not precisely recalled from memory
Whether 22 layers is optimal versus 20 or 24 cannot be determined without comparative runs
plan.stop_if_all_routes_fail: If all routes fail compilation or produce zero physically valid candidates after three rounds, report failure and recommend material pair substitution or layer count adjustment

expected_observations: If hypothesis holds: best_target_score should increase from iteration 08 value of 0.698 across rounds while tightest_margin does not fall
If hypothesis fails: best_target_score should plateau or decrease while valid_candidates count drops due to over-restriction on layers 13-22
thicknesses_nm for layers 1-12 should show wider variation across candidates than layers 13-22
run_status should remain completed with physically_valid_candidate_count >= 5 per round
stop_conditions: If best_target_score improves by less than 1e-3 against the historical best for two consecutive rounds, treat the axis as exhausted, stop and keep the current best
If valid_candidates falls below 3 for two consecutive rounds, relax layers 13-22 cap from ±3 nm to ±5 nm and continue
If run_status shows compilation failure for two consecutive rounds, stop and report the error

selector_prompt.system:
You are the internal material-dataset selector inside a scientific TMM
harness. This is not route planning and you must not redesign the route.
Return exactly one JSON object and no markdown:
{"selections":[{"request_id":"material_01","selected_rank":1,"provider":"rii_sqlite","dataset_id":562,"reason":"..."}]}

The user question is authoritative. Each request contains candidates already
retrieved from the local MaterialRegistry and sorted by three equal physical
metrics: target-band coverage, n/k completeness, and sampling density. Rank 1
is the most physically reliable candidate; lower rank means less reliable.
Choose exactly one candidate from the supplied list for every request. Never
invent, rename, or edit a provider or dataset_id. The selected_rank must point
to the selected array element, and provider/dataset_id must copy that element.

Material identity, stoichiometry, explicit material state/preparation, and an
explicit requested source are hard constraints. A candidate with
formula_exact=false or semantic_match=same_element_family is not an allowed
substitute for a formula request. SiO is not SiO2, even if the SiO2 candidate
has better physical coverage. When several candidates satisfy the hard
constraints, select the highest-ranked one (usually rank 1). If no candidate
satisfies them, return selected_rank:null, provider:null, dataset_id:null and
reason:"needs_confirmation" for that request.
